blanks.sentence: Real police investigations are different from what people often see on _____.
Solving crimes involves collecting and reviewing lots of _____.
This work takes a lot of _____.
Alastair is interested in AI because his professional background is in _____.
When officers review large amounts of information, it can be hard to find useful _____.
AI may improve police _____ by speeding up this work.
There is renewed _____ in pattern-recognition evidence.
This type of evidence became less popular partly because of interest in _____.
A possible concern is that AI would require collecting lots of _____.

multipleChoice.question: How are real police investigations described in the programme?
options: They are usually the same as television murder mysteries.
They depend mainly on one detective’s personality.
They involve practical evidence-gathering and review.
They are mostly solved by guessing the criminal’s motive.

multipleChoice.question: What problem could AI help with in police work?
options: Making police investigations more entertaining.
Reducing the time needed to review evidence.
Replacing all traditional forms of evidence.
Deciding whether a crime has happened.

multipleChoice.question: Why is Alastair interested in artificial intelligence?
options: He works in policing and has investigation experience.
He designs fictional detective programmes.
He is building a robot detective.
He wants to replace police training completely.

multipleChoice.question: What does Alastair mean by asking “What can it do for me?”
options: He wants to know how AI may be practically useful.
He wants AI to explain its personal opinions.
He is asking whether AI can watch detective dramas.
He is unsure what artificial intelligence means.

multipleChoice.question: What is difficult when police officers have a lot of information to review?
options: Knowing what matters and finding relevant patterns.
Choosing which television detective to copy.
Avoiding all forms of forensic science.
Taking photographs with mobile phones.

multipleChoice.question: What development does Ruth Morgan describe?
options: A new interest in evidence based on recognising patterns.
A complete end to the use of fingerprints.
A move away from all forensic science.
A system where witnesses replace physical evidence.

multipleChoice.question: Why did pattern-recognition evidence become less popular for a time?
options: DNA evidence attracted more excitement.
Police officers stopped collecting physical evidence.
Databases became illegal in all investigations.
Marks from shoes and fingers disappeared.

multipleChoice.question: How could AI make marks from a crime scene useful?
options: By comparing a photo of a mark with a database quickly.
By asking witnesses to describe the mark from memory.
By changing the mark to match a suspect.
By removing the need to collect evidence.

multipleChoice.question: What is the broader benefit of AI when dealing with evidence patterns?
options: It can make pattern-finding quicker and more dependable.
It can prove that every suspect is guilty.
It can remove the need for human police officers immediately.
It can stop crimes before they happen.

multipleChoice.question: What concern is raised about using AI to solve crimes?
options: It may require access to large amounts of private information.
It cannot recognise any kind of physical evidence.
It would make databases too slow to use.
It would make DNA evidence more popular.
